Types of Tooth Extractions Offered at Valencia Smile Expert
Not all tooth extractions are the same. At Valencia Smile Expert, we perform two main types of extractions depending on the condition and location of the tooth:

children.title: Simple Extractions
children.desc: Used when a tooth is fully visible in the mouth and can be removed without surgical intervention. These are typically performed on teeth that are loose or damaged beyond repair.

children.title: Surgical Extractions
children.desc: Required for teeth that are impacted, broken at the gumline, or not fully erupted—like many wisdom teeth. Surgical extractions involve making a small incision in the gum and may require sectioning the tooth for easier removal.

children.html: Who Might Need a Tooth Extraction?

Tooth extractions are typically a last resort—but when a tooth poses a risk to your oral health or daily comfort, removal can provide lasting relief and prevent further complications. You may be a good candidate for a tooth extraction if you’re experiencing:

items.text: Severe tooth decay that cannot be repaired with a filling, crown, or root canal
Infection or abscess that has spread to the pulp or surrounding bone
Impacted wisdom teeth causing pain, swelling, or shifting of other teeth
Advanced periodontal disease that has loosened the tooth’s foundation
Overcrowding that interferes with orthodontic treatment or bite alignment
Cracked or fractured teeth beyond restoration due to trauma or grinding

children.html: Benefits of Tooth Extraction From Valencia Smile Expert

children.title: Elimination of Infection

children.title: Protection for Surrounding Teeth

children.html: How to Care for Your Mouth Before and After a Tooth Extraction

Proper care before and after your extraction helps ensure a smooth procedure and quick, comfortable healing. At Valencia Smile Expert, we provide personalized guidance every step of the way so you can feel confident and cared for.
Before Your Extraction:

items.text: Avoid smoking or alcohol for at least 24 hours prior
Let us know about any medications or health conditions
Eat a light meal (unless sedation is planned)
Arrange transportation if you’ll be receiving sedation
Practice good oral hygiene to reduce infection risk

children.html: After Your Extraction:

items.text: Rest for the first 24 hours and avoid strenuous activity
Don’t use straws, smoke, or spit forcefully, as this can dislodge the blood clot and cause dry socket
Stick to soft, cool foods like yogurt, smoothies, scrambled eggs, or mashed potatoes
Use ice packs and take any prescribed medications to manage swelling and discomfort
Rinse gently with saltwater after the first 24 hours to keep the area clean

FAQs About Tooth Extractions

items.title: Is getting a tooth pulled painful?

children.html: Most patients are surprised at how quick and comfortable the procedure is. We use local anesthesia to numb the area completely, and sedation options are available if you’re feeling anxious. You may feel some pressure—but not pain—during the extraction.

items.title: How long does it take to recover after a tooth extraction?

children.html: Initial healing typically takes 1–3 days for simple extractions, and about a week for surgical ones. Most patients return to normal activities within a few days, following proper aftercare.

items.title: What can I eat after a tooth extraction?

children.html: Stick to soft, cool foods for the first couple of days—think yogurt, smoothies, applesauce, and scrambled eggs. Avoid straws, crunchy snacks, or anything too hot until the area has started to heal.

items.title: Do I need to replace a tooth after it’s extracted?

children.html: In most cases, yes—especially if the extracted tooth isn’t a wisdom tooth. Missing teeth can cause neighboring teeth to shift and affect your bite. We can discuss options like dental implants, bridges, or partial dentures during your follow-up.
